cells.value: This tab shows where each AI (Claude Code, the Claude app, Codex, ChatGPT and Cursor) finds its skills, the size and count limits, how many skills to keep on, how to prove a skill loaded, and the house rules. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that teaches an AI one procedure. Every row names its source in the last column, and NOT_PROVEN marks what still needs a check. The tab is built by work/2026-10-01_setup-playbook/build_tabs.py from tabs/skills-where.json; never edit the sheet by hand.

Global home: ~/.agents/skills (this Mac)
The one real copy of every shared skill. A skill is a folder holding a SKILL.md file (its instructions). On 2026-10-01 it held 122 skill folders.

Create or edit the skill here, never inside an app's own folder. unify.py moves stray copies here and turns identical Claude copies into links (pointers to the real folder). Retired copies are moved to ~/skills-archive, never deleted.
It is a folder, not an AI. Codex and Cursor read it directly. Claude Code reaches it through the links in ~/.claude/skills. The Claude app and ChatGPT never read it.

Claude Code (terminal and the desktop app's Code tab)

Personal skills in ~/.claude/skills (links into ~/.agents/skills), the project's .claude/skills, plugin skills (skills inside an installed plugin, named plugin:skill), and skills uploaded to the Claude app. The desktop Code tab gets the uploads in-process as anthropic-skills:<name>. The terminal gets them only on version 2.1.273 or later, synced one way into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ at start and about every 10 minutes.
Add a link in ~/.claude/skills (picked up live, no restart), or upload to the Claude app and let it sync. One delivery per skill: an uploaded skill gets no ~/.claude/skills link (section 5).

A skill listing (every name plus its 'when to use me' description) is in every session; Claude matches the request against it, or you type /name. If a local and a synced skill share a name, the local one is /name and the synced one is /anthropic-skills:name.

Local folders: .agents/skills from the current folder up to the repo root, ~/.agents/skills, /etc/codex/skills and the bundled ~/.codex/skills/.system. Plus plugin skills from ~/.codex/plugins/cache, named plugin:skill (the IDE extension takes no plugins). Codex follows links and also scans nested folders, so template copies inside a skill get listed too.

Put a folder with SKILL.md in a scanned place, or install a plugin and start a new session. Don't use $skill-installer: it writes to ~/.codex/skills, a third home. To hide a skill from Codex only, add an off-switch ([[skills.config]] with its path and enabled = false) to ~/.codex/config.toml, then restart.

A catalog (each skill's name, description and path) goes into the prompt. Pick with $name, /skills or the Skills picker, or Codex picks by description. A skill set to allow_implicit_invocation: false in agents/openai.yaml loads only when named.

SKILL.md body (and its references/ files)

Our target: 60 lines / 5,000 characters. Our cap: 200 lines / 16,000 characters. Each references/ file: 300 lines / 25,000 characters, one level deep. Outside guidance (Anthropic, Agent Skills standard): under 500 lines and about 5,000 tokens.
Every skill on every AI. repo-conform checks the body limits when it audits a project; references/ sizes were not measured yet.

Claude Code keeps only the first 5,000 tokens of a skill after compaction (when it shrinks a long session). In SkillsBench, skill text over about 43 KB per task gained only +0.7 points. Move detail into references/. The house README states the same limits since repo-conform 2.2 (2026-10-01); before that it said 150 lines.

Any surface (setup)

Add one canary line (a marker) at the end of the skill's body, not its description: 'When you use this skill, end your reply with [skill:<name> <date>]'. Change the date each time the skill is updated. Record every result as date | surface | prompt | canary Y/N in the job's checks.md.

The marker in a reply proves the whole SKILL.md loaded, not just its name and description. The marker means the same thing in the Claude app and Claude Code: both load only a skill's name and description until it is used, then the whole SKILL.md. No T2 to T4 run is recorded on either surface yet.
